text:
Loved the recent article on evals from @HamelHusain
and @sh_reya in the  @lennysan newsletter. One question we get everytime with PMs is what evals to write for long horizon agents that do a broad swath of work (what H/S call error discovery, similar to product discovery).   

Below is a great framework for how you can organize these discoveries as a product team: 
1️⃣ Outcome - were the results great
2️⃣ Trajectory - was the process followed correct
3️⃣ Experience - did it feel right 
4️⃣ Governance - did it follow critical rules 

You start with your product pov, but the only way to hone focus is to look at traces (trace analysis). Here's an example of an annotated trace for a local shopping assistant called Corner and how often the trace reveals flaws before they become obvious to the customer. 

https://t.co/iYpCvt1etN

text:
Thariq from Anthropic's Claude Code team just published his tests on effort: turning effort up mostly buys 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗲-𝗰𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴. You can turn his approach into 𝘁𝘄𝗼 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 and have Claude Code follow it.

For new features, he works in four steps:
→ Have Claude ask you questions first and fill in what the spec is missing
→ Build it on low. It's fast, and you can step in anytime
→ Look it over, and if it needs changes, stay on low
→ Switch to high at the end to verify and test

If you want to try it, send this image and the prompt below to Claude Code 👇

"Set up the workflow in this image in my Claude Code:

1. Create two subagents in ~/.claude/agents:
- builder: writes the code. model: opus, effort: low. It implements the spec I've approved and stops when it's done.
- verifier: checks the work. model: opus, effort: high. It runs the feature first to see what it actually does, then adds tests, focusing on edge cases. It reports problems to me and doesn't change the code itself.

2. Add a rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: when I ask for a new feature, first ask me what the spec is missing; after I confirm, hand it to builder; after I've reviewed the result, hand it to verifier.

3. Check whether the environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL is set. If it is, the effort settings on both subagents won't take effect. Just tell me; don't change it.

Show me the contents of the files you'll create or change, then explain the whole workflow in words a 10-year-old could follow. Don't write anything until I confirm."

text:
我草，GitHub 现在已经卷成这样了

这 7 个开源项目，一个比一个狠，让我在KTV尖叫，都是神器！

拿它查人，查公司，扫设备，还有一个直接想把导演、编剧、制片全干掉

1、Aliens Eye

输入一个用户名，直接横扫 840+ 平台，几秒跑完，还支持代理、Tor、多格式导出

https://t.co/woB8qwyqLG

2、Blackbird

一个用户名 / 邮箱，直接查数百个平台，直接帮你把不同平台上的公开身份痕迹串起来

很多人第一次跑自己，才发现原来网上早就留下了一长串脚印

https://t.co/XOOtN4KPYh

3、Maigret

用户名追踪界的怪物，覆盖 3000+ 网站

你以为只查一个 ID？

能顺着发现的关联用户名继续往下挖，一层套一层，公开痕迹越多，越容易被串起来

https://t.co/65nzOWq1Zp

4、SpiderFoot

这个已经不是“查资料”了，一堆零散线索，瞬间变成一张网。

手机号、邮箱、域名、IP、子域名、公开泄露信息一起吃，200+ 模块并行跑

https://t.co/LiPxYuWb15

5、theHarvester

扔进去一个域名，邮箱、子域名、IP、URL 等公开信息会被一批批拉出来。

查公司公开资产非常狠，很多公司以为自己只是上线了一个官网，结果就被扒出来了

https://t.co/QltiLJ0eVI

6、Shodan Python

服务器、路由器、摄像头、IoT 设备，只要暴露在公网，就可能被搜到。

真正可怕的不是工具。

是很多设备上线几年了，配置从来没人检查过。

https://t.co/Nrw13OXY6N

7、ViMax

这个更狠，港大做的多 Agent 视频系统

你给它一个想法、一段剧本，甚至一本小说，它就开始自己拆剧情、管角色、做分镜、生成视频

导演、编剧、分镜、制片……

以前是一条制作团队，现在正在被压成一条 Agent 流水线

https://t.co/N0FOQPPluM

quotedTweet.text:
JEV + OPUS 5.5 是我今年见过最离谱的 AI 组合

别在让 Opus 5.5 干所有活，真的太浪费了

我直接做一个 X 爆款预测器：

抓取 1000 条爆款帖子 → Jev 做上万次特征判断 → 找出最相似的 10 条 → Opus 5.5 解释为什么它们能爆 → 最后给你的帖子打出 0-100 分

新工作流只有一句话：

Jev 负责做 5,000 次判断，Opus 5.5 只负责最难的 20 次推理，效果直接变了，基本每天爆款

审计里，Jev 不到 1 分钟 扫完 600+ 页面，完成接近 9,000 次链接判断，总成本只要 几毛钱。

同样时间，Opus 只能处理 20 多页，成本已经高出数倍。

全部交给 Opus 跑完，成本可能直接放大到 40 美元，差距接近 200 倍

这也是我写的贴流量几十万播放的的主要原因

My FULL architecture for building an AI trading bot with Claude Code:

(three simple steps)

1. Tool stack

You need three things to build a bot with Claude:

a) Claude Code on desktop installed and running
b) An account with any exchange that has a public MCP
c) Your account API key (generate a new one)

Tell Claude Code to connect these three things in a new project.

Once connected, Claude can read market data, place orders, check positions, and manage risk from plain English.

Step 2. Write your strategy

Tell Claude to create a new CLAUDE.md file and describe your market strategy:

• Entry/exit rules
• Risk caps and position sizing
• Allowed pairs
• Execution protocol

Pro tip: I recommend voice prompting here to really extract all the necessary data

Step 3. Add a risk gate

Before going live, ask Claude Code to set these up:

• Kill switch - halts all trading instantly if triggered
• Daily loss cap
• Notional cap - no single order above [x]% NAV
• Leverage cap -no single order above [x] leverage

text:
After a lot of procrastination and preparation, I finally dug out my old trading-theory notes and trading-algo drafts and wrote Part 2 of my series on futures trading methodology…

In Part 1, I laid out the mathematical structure of $ES, $NQ and $VIX futures and how they work.

The new post, part 2 goes from reading a volume profile all the way to a working order:
- What volume and TPO profiles actually measure, and what they don't: traded volume is not order-book liquidity
- How to read the open and the developing auction: prior value, the first 15 minutes, the opening price as the intraday pivot, and the 4 classic opening sequences
- How to scale entries, stops and targets to the day's realized volatility instead of fixed point distances
- 3 precisely defined entry models: a failed excursion back into value, continuation away from value (including going with an opening drive), and expansion from an intraday balance
- A real September 23 ES short, step by step: confirmation, entry, position sizing from the worst permitted fill, execution in IBKR, and 2 different exit policies from the same entry, showing why the exit matters as much as the entry
- And the part most people skip: how little a single winning trade proves, how many trades a track record really needs, and how execution costs quietly eat a "good" reward-to-risk ratio

Along the way I walk through the implementation of my 2 TradingView indicators, HTF Lvls (completed-period POC, value area and VWAP levels) and RV (intraday realized volatility and its rank), including the math behind them and their blind spots.

The rules are a frame, not a machine. They are precise enough to test and log, but meant to discipline judgment, not to replace it.

In the next part, I'll move from the profile to the swing, talking about the 3/10 oscillator, first crosses and divergences across time frames, the rhythm of buy, sell and sell-short days, classic setups (Holy Grail, three-bar triangle, pinball, failure tests), extended runs, market internals (TICK, breadth, volume), and trade management: initial stops, scaling out, runners and re-entry.
And I'll finish it with the practical implementation of the implied probability distribution that I discovered how one can distract from market and positioning datas as the only forward-looking model based on factual datas. 

All of it the way I once learned it from my mentors, one of whom appears in the Market Wizards series.

Enjoy the read, and happy learning!
Warmly, 
~A❤️

分享一套免费、开源的 MDX 文档组件集「mdxcn」：包含提示框、步骤、终端、图表和时间线等 Markdown 友好型组件，可通过 shadcn CLI 一条命令复制进项目使用。
 
作者 @kshvbgde 
官网 https://t.co/qyIYs5FT6O
开源 https://t.co/8q2Dr1QEEe

写重构方案、事故复盘、PR 说明时，「一堵要点的 bullet 墙」读起来慢，而一张图扫一眼就懂。它的解法并不是引入 Mermaid 或 SVG 图表，是用纯字符（█ ░ - = + ├ └）画出带虚线边框、左上角 + 号包角、顶边标注 [ TITLE ] 的图表。

这个选择带来一个关键优势：图表就是纯文本。重新打开 MDX 文件时，标签和数值依然可读，Agent 也能像当初写它一样直接编辑这帧图：不依赖渲染器，不产生二进制资产。

视觉语法（强制约束）
· 字体 Geist Mono；边框一律虚线；明确禁用 SVG、Mermaid、Recharts、canvas，也禁止发明自制 ASCII 或饼图
· 单一强调色，通过 --graph-accent 注入；palette="duo"|"multi" 为显式 opt-in
· 动效仅限 opacity/transform、约 220ms、无循环无脉冲

最独特的设计：双轨交付
这是 mdxcn 区别于普通组件库的地方，它同时是「给人用的组件包」和「给 Agent 用的 Skills」：
1. 安装：pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add https://t.co/KM4Sm4xZqw，源码落入 @/registry/default；skill 则装进 Agent 本来就会读取的目录
2. 工作流：装好 skill 后直接「要一份 write-up」→ 内置的 chooser（决策表）按写作目的和数据形态挑选图表（如事后复盘 → GraphTimeline + GraphUptime；前后数值对比 → GraphSlope）→ 从文档复制 props、替换标签即成
3. 纪律约束：每次最多两张图、图之间必须有正文、标题 1–2 个词全大写无标点、正文先于图出现

多宿主输出策略
同一张图针对不同目标输出不同格式，且规则明确：React/MDX 出 JSX；Comark 应用出 ::graph-* YAML 块；Knap 模板出 graph_* filter；而 Notion、Linear、README、GitHub 等纯 Markdown 场景直接贴官方围栏 ASCII。文档反复强调禁止错配，例如 ::graph-* 贴进 GitHub 不会渲染。

result.text:
分享一套免费、开源的 MDX 文档组件集「mdxcn」：包含提示框、步骤、终端、图表和时间线等 Markdown 友好型组件，可通过 shadcn CLI 一条命令复制进项目使用。
 
作者 @kshvbgde 
官网 https://t.co/qyIYs5FT6O
开源 https://t.co/8q2Dr1QEEe

写重构方案、事故复盘、PR 说明时，「一堵要点的 bullet 墙」读起来慢，而一张图扫一眼就懂。它的解法并不是引入 Mermaid 或 SVG 图表，是用纯字符（█ ░ - = + ├ └）画出带虚线边框、左上角 + 号包角、顶边标注 [ TITLE ] 的图表。

这个选择带来一个关键优势：图表就是纯文本。重新打开 MDX 文件时，标签和数值依然可读，Agent 也能像当初写它一样直接编辑这帧图：不依赖渲染器，不产生二进制资产。

视觉语法（强制约束）
· 字体 Geist Mono；边框一律虚线；明确禁用 SVG、Mermaid、Recharts、canvas，也禁止发明自制 ASCII 或饼图
· 单一强调色，通过 --graph-accent 注入；palette="duo"|"multi" 为显式 opt-in
· 动效仅限 opacity/transform、约 220ms、无循环无脉冲

最独特的设计：双轨交付
这是 mdxcn 区别于普通组件库的地方，它同时是「给人用的组件包」和「给 Agent 用的 Skills」：
1. 安装：pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add https://t.co/KM4Sm4xZqw，源码落入 @/registry/default；skill 则装进 Agent 本来就会读取的目录
2. 工作流：装好 skill 后直接「要一份 write-up」→ 内置的 chooser（决策表）按写作目的和数据形态挑选图表（如事后复盘 → GraphTimeline + GraphUptime；前后数值对比 → GraphSlope）→ 从文档复制 props、替换标签即成
3. 纪律约束：每次最多两张图、图之间必须有正文、标题 1–2 个词全大写无标点、正文先于图出现

多宿主输出策略
同一张图针对不同目标输出不同格式，且规则明确：React/MDX 出 JSX；Comark 应用出 ::graph-* YAML 块；Knap 模板出 graph_* filter；而 Notion、Linear、README、GitHub 等纯 Markdown 场景直接贴官方围栏 ASCII。文档反复强调禁止错配，例如 ::graph-* 贴进 GitHub 不会渲染。

text:
ANTHROPIC JUST DROPPED A 12-TIP MANUAL FOR PROMPTING CLAUDE OPUS 5.5

And almost everything you know about prompting Claude is now wrong.

The mistake everyone is making?

Prompting Opus 5.5 like Opus 5.

More instructions. More guardrails. More control.

Opus 5.5 needs the opposite.

→ "think step by step" - delete it, you're adding latency not quality
→ "show your reasoning" - gets declined now, it's in your prompts already
→ medium effort - matches Opus 5 at high, you're overpaying by default
→ CLAUDE.md - rewrite it for autonomy, not supervision
→ task checklist - it mistakes progress updates for finish lines
→ time budget - two words and it paces itself to finish faster
→ free reset - expiring in Settings right now and you don't know

Three things that will surprise you:

→ the effort level you're running is almost certainly wrong
→ the prompts making it stop early are ones you wrote on purpose
→ removing 40 lines from your CLAUDE.md will make it perform better

Opus 5 → More Control
Opus 5.5 → Clear Goal → Autonomy → Verification → Done

This is not a model you improve by adding more.

It's a model you unlock by taking away.

Full 12-tip manual. Every prompt copy-paste ready.

Read this before you touch another CLAUDE.md ↓

Bookmark before your next session.

text:
Chinese students just found the best way to use JEV for any LLM or AI agent - released a PDF research

the shift: I pasted it into Claude and GPT - and cut my costs by~63х

here’s what they found across 44 benchmarks:

1 → 7,193 responses, 10 types of failure. Jev was tested on hallucinations, prompt injections, data leaks, and other AI failures

2 → One simple question worked: 0.886 median AUROC, beating trained baselines on 25 of 31 benchmarks without task-specific training

3 → Context beat clever prompting - give Jev the source or rule it needs to check the answer against

4 → Keep the probability, not just "yes" or "no" - Fitting a threshold on 10 labeled examples raised median F1 from 0.706 to 0.793

5 → Among the 50% most confident decisions, median accuracy reached 0.933 - send uncertain cases for another review

6 → Jev even helped uncover labeling errors in three benchmarks. Sometimes the test’s "correct answer" was the problem

7 → 11.4 questions per call, with 0.31-second median latency - on 19 benchmarks, checking cost $0.30 vs $18.96 with LLM judges - roughly 63× cheaper

the result: It will made your setup CHEAPER and FASTER than what 95% of people are running

Copy the Jev setup researchers tested across 44 benchmarks - then read the full Jev architecture ↓

text:
Fuck it, still early but here goes ...

We've just released Monty v1 - a Python sandbox that starts in 1 millisecond, not 1.5 seconds.

I just ran 10k sandboxed scripts in 674ms, something that would take a cloud sandbox > 3 hours.

This removes the biggest drawback of letting agents write code. The future is fast.

Even better, it's open source, you can install it from PyPI, npm or Crates now.

Serviced platform coming soon. Please get in touch if you want to be a design partner!

Who should try it?

⚡ if you care about startup time, use Monty
⚡ if you care about long-lived sessions, use Monty - Monty can be dumped and resumed at any external function call
⚡ if you care about accessing functions in the agent/host, use Monty - Monty makes it trivial to expose local functions into the sandbox
⚡ if you care about scale, use Monty - Monty workers use as little as 2MB of memory, meaning you can run thousands of concurrent sandboxes on a single machine
⚡ if you care about security, use Monty - we've run 3 rounds of bounty program and thousands of researchers have tried to break into our sandbox, meaning it should be secure to run untrusted code

Who should avoid it?

🚫 if you like to take a coffee break while waiting for sandboxes to start, DO NOT use Monty
🚫 if you enjoy the challenge of routing API requests from sandboxes through your corporate network to access state in your agent without exposing secrets to the sandbox, DO NOT use Monty
🚫 if your agent really needs to install packages from PyPI, Monty won't help you yet (spoiler: it probably doesn't)

https://t.co/avO8TWY5gJ

Someone open-sourced a crypto trading bot on GitHub, completely free.

It’s called Cabbage: a spot trading bot you can backtest, paper-trade, or run live with one command.

Astra (GPT-6) built it. Jev runs it.

Astra handles the reasoning and code. Jev returns one decision in milliseconds: BUY, HOLD, or SELL. Below 0.80 confidence, it waits.

1.⁠ ⁠Signal engine
   RSI 14 + EMA 12/26 confluence using closed candles only.

2.⁠ ⁠Hard risk rules
   Fixed position size + percentage stop-loss on every entry.

3.⁠ ⁠Backtesting
   Replays historical candles one by one and generates a full HTML report.

4.⁠ ⁠Paper trading
   Uses live exchange data with simulated fills and zero money at risk.

5.⁠ ⁠Live trading
   Places real orders through any exchange supported by CCXT.

6.⁠ ⁠Doctor command
   Checks your config and exchange connection before any trade is placed.

State is stored in SQLite per market and pair, so restarting doesn’t wipe your positions.

Built on Investing Algorithm Framework 9. Apache-2.0.

Fork it and make it yours.

⁠ https://t.co/fpuIdcLBnY ⁠

text:
The hedge fund manager who taught Michael Burry to pick stocks accidentally destroyed the mutual fund industry in a free Talks at Google lecture on the two-line formula that turned $10,000 into $8.3 million.

His fund charged 2 and 20. He gave the strategy away in a $12 book.

Almost no one paying a financial advisor 1 percent of their retirement has finished the lecture.

His name is Joel Greenblatt. He founded Gotham Capital in 1985 and compounded roughly 40 percent a year for twenty consecutive years. He returned all outside capital in 1994 because his edge was too crowded to scale.

He has been teaching value investing at Columbia Business School every year since 1996. Michael Burry - the doctor who shorted the housing bubble in "The Big Short" - learned to pick stocks from Greenblatt's 1997 book.

The 55-minute clip in this video is Greenblatt at Google in 2017 walking a room of engineers through his Magic Formula.

The whole framework fits on one napkin. Rank every stock in the S&P 500 by return on invested capital, highest first. Then rank every stock by earnings yield, highest first. Sum the two rankings. Buy the top twenty. Hold for one year. Sell. Repeat.

That single formula would have beaten the S&P 500 by roughly 14 percent a year over the last three decades if any retail investor had actually followed it.

"Cheap and good beats expensive and average. Every time."

That is Joel Greenblatt at Google in 2017. He has repeated the sentence in every public talk since. Almost no retail investor buying Nvidia at $140 has heard it.

Every hedge fund on Wall Street pays $500,000-a-year analysts to backtest more sophisticated versions of the same equation. Every financial advisor in America charges you 1 percent of your account per year to underperform it.

The Talks at Google video is free on YouTube. "The Little Book That Beats the Market" is twelve dollars on Amazon.

Almost none of the millions who watched have ever run the two-line formula on their own portfolio.

The framework is free. The willingness to actually run it before your next stock pick, retirement rebalance, or brokerage transfer is the entire edge.

text:
Banger paper from Microsoft and colleagues.

We talk about human taste being important in this AI era.

But for recursive self-improvement, an agent's taste also matters.

The big question is: How often do frontier agents pick the better direction at a decision point in a long task?

It's apparently just under 60% of the time, according to Taste-Bench.

In this benchmark, each question shows a point in a trajectory where several directions are open, and one leads to a better outcome.

The forks are mined automatically from parallel attempts and detours in engineering and research runs.

The best model answers 59.7% correctly.

Forks whose deciding evidence appears later in the trajectory are much harder, and a larger reasoning budget does not raise accuracy.

The authors then distill a teacher's judgment of the outcome into a student model, which improves end-to-end success on held-out SWE-bench Pro tasks.

Paper: https://t.co/uLoZWXiepY

text:
很多做独立开发或者轻量工具的朋友，项目还没几个真实用户，每个月先把云服务器、托管数据库和对象存储的固定账单付了一轮。

其实如果摸透 Cloudflare 的现代开发者生态，从前端展示、后端接口、数据存储到后台重型计算，全套业务链路都可以用边缘免运维方案串起来。

前端展示层直接交给 Pages 或者 Workers 静态资产托管。
不管是 React、Vue 还是 TanStack 编译出来的静态文件，直接关联 GitHub 仓库。每次 git push 自动触发构建和全球分发。免费额度不限制流量和访问请求次数，一个月送 500 次自动化构建，足够日常高频发版。

后端日常接口用 Workers 配 Hono。
Hono 本身体积极小，原生契合 V8 隔离沙箱，冷启动速度都在毫秒级。业务代码用 TypeScript 写，还能通过 RPC 机制跟前端直接共用类型定义。免费版每天给 100,000 次请求，单次请求提供 10 毫秒的纯 CPU 运算时间。因为等待数据库读写和第三方 API 返回的网络耗时不算在 CPU 时间内，处理日常登录认证、业务调度和 Webhook 绰绰有余。

关系型数据用 D1 配合 Drizzle ORM。
D1 是跑在边缘底座上的分布式 SQLite，查点改非常轻快。免费层每天给 500 万行读取和 10 万行写入，单库上限 500MB，还自带 7 天时间旅行快照恢复。配合轻量级的 Drizzle ORM，类型提示顺手，没有重型 ORM 的运行开销。对于早期项目来说，每天几百万次数据读取基本用不完。

用户上传文件和媒体资源放在 R2。
这是很多开发者最喜欢的组件，兼容 S3 协议标准，代码迁移只需改一下端点配置。每个月提供 10GB 免费存储、100 万次写入和 1000 万次读取。最关键的一点是没有出网流量费，避开了传统云厂商最容易让人心惊胆战的流量账单陷阱。

高频缓存和开关配置塞进 KV。
它在全球边缘节点同步键值数据，读取延迟极低，每天有 100,000 次免费读请求。不过需要留意的是免费版每天只有 1,000 次写入额度，所以它适合放变更频率低但读取频繁的数据，比如接口限流规则、用户会话或者功能灰度开关，高频写入的流水数据依然要写进 D1。

如果业务真碰到了重型计算，比如要跑 Python 脚本、做音视频转码、执行持久长连接，或者给 AI 跑代码沙箱，也不用回去买传统服务器配 Kubernetes。

Cloudflare 官方已经提供了 Containers 容器平台。它的做法是用 Workers 和 Durable Objects 作为编排网关与生命周期调度器，把 Docker 容器直接塞进边缘网络。容器平时保持休眠，有重任务触发时按需唤醒，按实际执行的毫秒切片计费，跑完自动缩容到零。

轻量接口走 V8 隔离沙箱零成本硬抗流量，重型计算用容器按需唤醒即用即走，再配合本地 Wrangler 模拟器和开箱模板，一个人就能把整套产品的运维成本压到最低。

https://t.co/gtdQyFmJXt I wrote a command line program to test moving average crossover systems with multiple signal assets, traded assets, and moving average lengths. It is in Python but is pretty fast. When multiple systems are tested, in addition to reporting the best Sharpe ratio it reports a Sharpe ratio deflated by the effective # of systems tested. If you test moving average lengths from 2 through 200, since the systems are correlated, the effective # of systems is much lower than 199.

Given a matrix whose columns are strategy returns, you can use the average correlation of columns or the eigenvalue spectrum of the matrix to estimate the effective # of systems. I was surprised that the eigenvalue method gave a much lower estimate, but it seems more realistic.

From 2003 on, SPY returns have been higher on average when IEF is above rather than below a short-term moving average such as 20 days.

text:
Ten million people have watched a Stanford lecturer accidentally destroy the entire interview coaching industry.

He filmed the lecture in 2023 and it has been on YouTube ever since.

Interview coaches charge three thousand dollars a session to teach a diluted version of what he covered in 44 minutes for free.

His name is Matt Abrahams. He is a lecturer at the Stanford Graduate School of Business, host of the "Think Fast, Talk Smart" podcast, and the coach every top Silicon Valley founder hires before their IPO roadshow.

Every year at Stanford's Alumni Weekend, he opens with the same six-step framework.

His entire framework fits on a napkin.

Anxiety is not a bug. Greet it. Belly-breathe and exhale twice as long. Cool your palms with a cold bottle before you walk in. Ground yourself in the current second. Never wing an answer. Use What, So What, Now What when your brain freezes. Problem, Solution, Benefit for a pitch.

That last rule alone has probably cost the interview coaching industry a hundred million dollars.

"You will not be judged on the words you rehearsed. You will be judged on the words you did not."

That is the actual opening line of the lecture. Abrahams built his entire 2023 book on the sentence.

Founders spend $50,000 on media training and freeze the moment the reporter asks the one question the coach did not rehearse. Executives walk into board meetings having prepared every slide and lose the deal on the follow-up they never anticipated.

The lecture is free on the Stanford Alumni YouTube channel. Abrahams's book "Think Faster, Talk Smarter" is under twenty dollars.

Abrahams still teaches at Stanford. Almost none of the ten million viewers have taken a single belly breath before their next question.

The frame is free. The willingness to actually breathe and use it the next time someone puts you on the spot is the entire edge.

text:
Anthropic 开始让 Claude 优化 Claude 自己了，而且两周就把核心使用体验提速了约 3 倍。

这次最值得看的，是他们怎么把 Claude 真正塞进性能工程闭环。

先把「哪里慢」变成可测的指标，再让 Claude 找瓶颈、建 Benchmark、改代码、跑验证，最后把这些指标接进 CI，防止性能再掉回去。

这里让我觉得很有价值的一点是，模型变强以后，工程效率越来越取决于你能不能给 Agent 一个清楚、可验证、可以持续反馈的目标。

只要反馈足够稳定，Agent 就能沿着这个闭环不断找问题、改方案、再验证。

这种工作方式以后可能会越来越常见。很多工程团队真正需要优化的，可能会慢慢变成「怎么把问题变成 Agent 能持续迭代的环境」。

文章： https://t.co/zcfjpmmcnt⁠

"JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure"

This paper shows you can just use JEV for every evaluation instead of expensive LLM.

JEV basically acts as a cheap first-pass judge, returning both a verdict and how confident it is. 

When confidence is high, keep the answer. When it’s low, escalate to a stronger LLM.

This simple routing keeps ~99% of GPT-6’s accuracy while reducing evaluation cost by a lot.

https://t.co/cP4EzOreaO

quotedTweet.text:
𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲 𝘁𝗶𝗽: once Opus 5.5 is your main model, don't let your Fable quota sit idle. Put Fable on call with /advisor.

Run /advisor fable and Claude Code gets 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀. Opus 5.5 keeps doing the work and usually calls Fable in at three moments:
→ Before committing to a plan: is it right?
→ When the same error keeps coming back: am I heading the wrong way?
→ Before saying "done": did I miss anything?
Fable reads the whole session and gives advice. Opus still writes the code.

The tree is the full setup. Opus 5.5 on high runs the main session. Three subagents on medium split the rest: one reads code, one edits and runs tests, one looks up docs. Fable waits on the sidelines. Hand the tree and this prompt to Claude Code to set it up 👇

"Set up my Claude Code to match this tree:
1. For the three subagents, reuse fitting ones from ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents, and propose new ones only for missing roles. Set each to model: opus and effort: medium. Leave any subagent that already sets a different model alone, and list it.
2. Set the main session's default effort to high with effortLevel in ~/.claude/settings.json.
3. Check for environment variables that turn the advisor off (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL, or DISABLE_TELEMETRY and anything else that stops flag fetching) and for CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, which overrides every subagent's effort. Report them; don't change them.
4. Add one rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: ask the advisor before committing to a big plan, when the same error shows up a second time, and before calling a long task done.

Show me the changes first. Don't edit any files yet."

https://t.co/FaFivbb9Pj

text:
Anthropic acaba de publicar un PDF de 13 páginas sobre memoria para agentes de IA

5 capas para reducir un 90% el coste en tokens y hacer que tu agente aprenda de verdad👇

1. MEMORIA DE TRABAJO: lo que ve ahora

La ventana de contexto. Todo lo que el agente tiene delante en este momento

Cuando se llena, el contexto antiguo se pierde. La mayoría de los agentes se quedan aquí y luego nos preguntamos por qué fallan

2. MEMORIA EPISÓDICA: lo que pasó

El historial completo de interacciones, con fecha y hora

El agente recuerda que el despliegue falló el martes a las 3 de la mañana porque el script de migración tenía una errata

No tienes que explicárselo otra vez

3. MEMORIA SEMÁNTICA: lo que sabe

Hechos, entidades y relaciones guardados en un grafo de conocimiento

«El usuario prefiere TypeScript» vive aquí

Y no desaparece cuando termina la sesión

4. MEMORIA PROCEDIMENTAL: cómo hacer las cosas

El agente prueba 3 enfoques. Uno funciona

Ese método se convierte en una habilidad reutilizable

La próxima vez va directamente a lo que funcionó

5. OLVIDO: lo que debe borrar

Un agente que nunca olvida acaba acumulando contradicciones

Las preferencias antiguas se imponen a las nuevas. Te mudas de ciudad y sigue recomendándote restaurantes donde vivías antes

Recordar importa. Saber qué olvidar, también

El resultado?

→ Mem0 almacena 1.800 tokens por consulta en lugar de 26.000
→ Snowflake añadió una capa de ontología: un 20% más de precisión y un 39% menos de llamadas a herramientas

La memoria compensa su coste desde el primer día

Este PDF de 13 páginas marca la diferencia entre un chatbot y un agente que aprende de verdad

No lo pases de largo👇

text:
Start a task in Claude Code. Finish it in Codex. You don't have to re-explain anything.

We just shipped beacon handoff in Beacon, our open-source, cross-harness memory layer for AI coding tools.

If you use more than one coding agent, you know the problem. You run out of credits, want a second opinion, or hit a task another model handles better. Then you start over and paste context back in by hand.

Now it's one command:
beacon handoff resume <session-id> --agent codex

What happens:
→ Beacon reads the session from the agent's own local store and writes a short handoff brief: what was asked, what changed, which commands ran, and where it stopped.
→ It starts Codex in the same directory, pointed at that brief.
→ Codex says what it understands the task to be and waits for your go-ahead before changing anything.
→ Beacon records a link between the two sessions in your local telemetry, so the trail stays connected.

It works across Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode and Cline, in any direction. It can also reopen a session natively in the same tool.

Everything stays on your machine. Nothing is uploaded, and secrets are redacted from the brief. The brief is passed by file path, never pasted into the command line.

In the video, Claude Code gets partway through summarizing a repo, and Codex finishes the job 👇

text:
On September 15, 2008, the Fed let Lehman Brothers go bankrupt. The next night it agreed to lend AIG $85 billion.

That Monday, MIT was filming a finance class. The professor ran Lehman's numbers, then his own mortgage, and told the room: "I beat Lehman Brothers."

An MIT Sloan MBA now costs $91,892 a year in tuition. This class, taught hours after the largest bankruptcy in US history, is free on YouTube.

His name is Andrew Lo. He runs MIT's Laboratory for Financial Engineering, and TIME named him one of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2012.

The video is the whole 72-minute session. At 3 a.m. that morning, Bank of America emailed to cancel its CFO's visit to MIT. That weekend the bank had passed on Lehman and agreed to buy Merrill Lynch.

What he taught that morning fits on the back of a mortgage statement.

Leverage is the price divided by your own money. 20% down is 5 to 1. His 5% down was 20 to 1, above the 16 to 1 on his Lehman slide. 3% down, which Fannie Mae offers first-time buyers, is 33 to 1.

The loss is yours alone. Put $100,000 down on a $500,000 house and let it fall 10%. Half your money is gone, and the bank still expects every dollar of its $400,000 back with interest.

Calm hides the risk. Home prices had climbed smoothly for years, which is what made his 20 to 1 feel safe.

Watch the reset. Owning is fine while you can pay. His example: a $300 teaser payment that becomes $1,000 a year later. That, he told the class, is what happened across the country.

Measure what your money buys. If your balance grows 10% and prices grow 10%, "You've made money, but you haven't made progress."

Leverage decides how small a drop can finish you. At 33 to 1, a 3% dip in price erases the entire down payment.

On September 15, 2008, the Fed let Lehman Brothers go bankrupt. The next night it agreed to lend AIG $85 billion.

That Monday, MIT was filming a finance class. The professor ran Lehman's numbers, then his own mortgage, and told the room: "I beat Lehman Brothers."

An MIT Sloan MBA now costs $91,892 a year in tuition. This class, taught hours after the largest bankruptcy in US history, is free on YouTube.

His name is Andrew Lo. He runs MIT's Laboratory for Financial Engineering, and TIME named him one of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2012.

The video is the whole 72-minute session. At 3 a.m. that morning, Bank of America emailed to cancel its CFO's visit to MIT. That weekend the bank had passed on Lehman and agreed to buy Merrill Lynch.

What he taught that morning fits on the back of a mortgage statement.

Leverage is the price divided by your own money. 20% down is 5 to 1. His 5% down was 20 to 1, above the 16 to 1 on his Lehman slide. 3% down, which Fannie Mae offers first-time buyers, is 33 to 1.

The loss is yours alone. Put $100,000 down on a $500,000 house and let it fall 10%. Half your money is gone, and the bank still expects every dollar of its $400,000 back with interest.

Calm hides the risk. Home prices had climbed smoothly for years, which is what made his 20 to 1 feel safe.

Watch the reset. Owning is fine while you can pay. His example: a $300 teaser payment that becomes $1,000 a year later. That, he told the class, is what happened across the country.

text:
写的挺好，我挺喜欢看不同的投资观点的。如果只看多头的，不看空头的，你是无法全面知道双方的论点依据是什么，从而做出自己的判断。
关于你对博通的看法，我觉得很有意思的一点就是，你把投资它比喻成年轻姑娘没必要把青春浪费在不值得的人身上，这话没错，时间成本的确也是成本，所以有人的投资风格就是炒趋势，买高动能股票，买瓶颈，这些都是短期内就能赚到钱的。
但同时风险也要考虑清楚，因为是炒动能和趋势，一旦市场冷静下来，或者叙事反转，那么之前暴涨的股票，也可能几天功夫就跌到低位，那么如果你追高进去，势必被套在高位。就好像年轻姑娘找对象，不能只图快和帅，还要花时间看清楚这个男人的本质，性格，是否能长期过日子。盲目下手的话，有可能耽误的时间更久。
说回投资，我往往会刻意避开这些高动能股票，或者尽量保持小仓位，尽量克制，比如我之前买的mrvl, credo, cls, intc这些高动能股票，我都保持在较小仓位，而且有了15%-20%的收益，我基本就会出掉，作为交易仓位，而不是长期投资仓位。
真正值得长期投资的，我往往会选择基本面扎实的，各自赛道的龙头公司，最好还是股价暂时在低位，被市场错配的股票。比如一年前的谷歌，半年前的meta, palantir，以及现在的英伟达和博通。
博通的CEO和CFO在多次正式场合重申过EPS在2028财年会达到30美元，市场短期内的确可以持有怀疑态度，连续两年增长超过60%是否可以实现。去验证这个说法，是需要几个月，甚至几个季度才能实现的。现在市场定价的是不愿相信，但一旦公司几个季度的财报的确显示EPS在往这个方向走，那么市场会很快意识到之前的错配，给出20倍PE不为过，那就是两年几乎翻倍的收益，给出30倍PE对于一家年度增长超过60%，定制芯片龙头公司来说也绝对不夸张，大家可以参考现在AMD的估值倍数，那么对应的就是900美元的博通，在2028年，也就是两年接近翻三倍。就算估值压倒只到一半，给15倍估值，那也是450美元的股票，对应的两年收益是28%，可能没有跑赢大盘，但绝对不至于赔钱，而且我认为这个情况发生的概率并不大。
至于EPS有没有可能有夸大的成分，有没有可能出现说的是30美元，到时候只有25美元甚至不到20美元，我只能说有这个可能，但可能性不大。博通的CEO, CFO分别在财报会议，以及之后CNBC的访谈中两次提到了2028财年30美元EPS的数据，如果他们没有很大把握，或者说这个30美元没有很大可见性的情况下，他们是绝对不会，也不敢乱说的。如果是信口胡吹的话，监管部门足够他们喝一壶的，甚至有可能遭到法律指控。
而且博通管理层的风格一项是如果提前看到了什么，会和媒体和盘托出。这样的好处是市场对他们的前瞻数字心里有底，方便估值。坏处就是每次财报，他们给出的数字和市场预测的往往非常接近，达不到财报结果大超预期，让市场兴奋的效果。这个风格是好是坏见仁见智，但至少有一点是可以肯定的，博通的管理层提出的明年20美元，后年30美元的指引，是有很高可信度的，只不过市场需要再看几次财报，才能证明这个路径。
投资一家公司，我会给出至少一年的时间去验证我最初的投资逻辑是否正确，每个人的风格不一样，情况也不一样，我拿来投资的钱，不是我几年内就需要的，所以我可以有这个时间跨度，但我也理解很多人会有不同的情况。但我认为，如果你投资的钱是几周或者几个月就需要用的话，那么股市风险还是太大了，因为短期的股价走向，谁也说不好。

text:
Jev founder Diogo Almeida introduced Jev as a model that returns typed answers with probabilities

That last part is where an agent can become more useful, or considerably more dangerous

A confident answer is not a correct answer. For Choice and Score, confidence tells you how concentrated the returned distribution is. It does not prove the evidence was complete, the policy was current or a tool call succeeded

I would build the gate this way:

step 1 → name the consequence of each route before picking a threshold

step 2 → let a low-stakes read tolerate more uncertainty than a refund, deletion or transfer

step 3 → treat a Noul near 0.5 as unresolved, not as a weak yes

step 4 → give the middle band a job: fetch missing evidence, ask for confirmation or queue review

step 5 → keep an escape route when none of the Choice options describes the case

step 6 → check permissions and hard policy in code even when the model is very sure

text:
如果你饱受睡眠和压力的困扰
可以看斯坦福神经科学家Andrew Huberman 
写的这本书：Protocols/《人体操作手册》。
主题：睡眠、运动、压力管理、营养、
光照、专注与学习、个人成长。
通过行为工具来获得长期健康
和身体效能，保持专注和学习效率
对高中生/大学生/成年人很有价值。
它不是传统的医学科普读物，
而是一本以神经科学和生理学为基础，
介绍如何调整日常行为、改善身心状态
及学习表现的实践手册。

睡眠：清晨5-30分钟的阳光直射眼睛；
醒来后30-60分钟的阳光照射有助于调节生物钟，
提升皮质醇水平，从而保持清醒并改善睡眠。

规律的起床时间；凉爽黑暗的卧室。 

压力：生理性叹息（双鼻吸气+长口呼气）1-3次。
通过副交感神经系统使肺泡重新扩张，降低心率。

运动：每天7-10千步。每周3次力量训练。
第二区间+高强度间歇训练（HIIT）。
每周2-4次灵活性训练。

营养：90%的天然食物。
每餐摄入约1克/磅体重的蛋白质。
早晨补充水分和蔬菜纤维。

光照：白天明亮/夜晚黑暗。

专注力：90分钟的专注训练+自然睡眠呼吸暂停（NSDR）。

从家长角度，可重点看
第6章：专注、动机和学习 
这一章比具体的健康技巧更适合成为
高中生理解“如何学习”的入口。
 
1. 为什么犯错是学习的重要组成部分？
书中强调，在真正尝试掌握新技能时，
错误能够提供反馈，
帮助人发现当前能力与目标之间的差距。
作者建议选择略高于现有能力的挑战，
而不是不断重复完全熟悉的任务。

一个学生可能把“做错题”理解为能力差，
但在学习新知识、创作和研究时，
错误也可以说明：
我在哪一步理解错了？
当前方法为什么行不通？
是否需要改变假设？
重要的并非刻意追求错误，
而是在真实尝试中学会使用反馈。 

2. 学习结束以后，
如何判断自己是否真正掌握？
作者在学习章节末尾提出，
可以在学习后花几分钟回忆刚刚接触的内容，
检查自己能记住什么、理解什么，
以及哪些地方仍然不清楚，
可以让朋友或ChatGPT帮助检查理解程度。
 
3. 目标、注意力与休息怎样配合？
作者讨论了学习前的心理准备、目标设定、
学习过程中的短暂休息，
以及睡眠对学习的作用。

text:
An MIT professor used two horses and $60,000 to expose how Wall Street gets paid without knowing which side will win.

One horse has a 20% chance of winning. The other has an 80% chance. The bookmaker knows the real probabilities, but the crowd does not. Bettors put $10,000 on the first horse and $50,000 on the second.

The professor asks one question: how can the bookmaker make the result irrelevant?

He ignores the probabilities and prices the flow of money instead. He offers five to one on the first horse and one to five on the second. If the first horse wins, the total payout is $60,000. If the second wins, it is still $60,000.

Exactly $60,000 came in. Exactly $60,000 goes out. Adjust the payouts slightly, and the difference becomes a guaranteed fee.

That is not gambling. It is engineered exposure.

The same logic sits underneath the derivatives market. Black-Scholes gets the headlines, but replication is the real machinery. You do not need to predict the future if you can construct a position that pays the same amount in every possible future.

The professor builds it on the board piece by piece. Take a derivative. Combine stock and cash until their payoff replicates the contract. Hold both sides. The directional risk disappears, and the pricing difference becomes yours.

Then he opens Bloomberg and does it with real IBM options. Using two calls at different strike prices, he constructs the payoff of a digital option. No story about where IBM is going. No heroic prediction. Just prices, payoffs and replication.

Professional traders repeat versions of this thousands of times a day. They enter a contract, hedge the exposure in the market and lock in the spread. They are not being paid for guessing the direction correctly. They are being paid for making direction irrelevant.

The amateur asks where the price will go. Wall Street asks how to get paid whichever way it moves.

The professor asks one question: how can the bookmaker make the result irrelevant?

He ignores the probabilities and prices the flow of money instead. He offers five to one on the first horse and one to five on the second. If the first horse wins, the total payout is $60,000. If the second wins, it is still $60,000.

Exactly $60,000 came in. Exactly $60,000 goes out. Adjust the payouts slightly, and the difference becomes a guaranteed fee.

That is not gambling. It is engineered exposure.

The same logic sits underneath the derivatives market. Black-Scholes gets the headlines, but replication is the real machinery. You do not need to predict the future if you can construct a position that pays the same amount in every possible future.

The professor builds it on the board piece by piece. Take a derivative. Combine stock and cash until their payoff replicates the contract. Hold both sides. The directional risk disappears, and the pricing difference becomes yours.

Then he opens Bloomberg and does it with real IBM options. Using two calls at different strike prices, he constructs the payoff of a digital option. No story about where IBM is going. No heroic prediction. Just prices, payoffs and replication.

Professional traders repeat versions of this thousands of times a day. They enter a contract, hedge the exposure in the market and lock in the spread. They are not being paid for guessing the direction correctly. They are being paid for making direction irrelevant.

The amateur asks where the price will go. Wall Street asks how to get paid whichever way it moves.

text:
Bonsai 2 27B 无限制版来了！12G 显卡就能跑，敏感提示词一条不拒，数学代码能力几乎没掉。

上周写 OrcaBonsai 时我说过，Bonsai 2 的权重只有 -1、0、+1，传统 abliteration 一改就得重新量化，能力容易掉。

这周一个日本个人开发者 Hikari，直接在 2-bit 编码上动刀。不转回浮点，不重新量化，改完的文件和原版一个字节都不差。

打个比方。别人是把一副理好的麻将推倒重洗，他是在牌桌上直接换牌，851 张换了 400 张，剩下 451 张一张没碰。

结果多狠？

40 条敏感提示词，原版拒 37 条，他的版本 0 条
数学、代码、工具调用小测，逐题一样
文件 7.2GB，12G 显卡就能跑

它凭什么改完不变笨？

每个编码只能整格跳，改不出细微的量。他用了无偏取整，让海量编码平均下来的移动，刚好等于想要的那一点修改。单看每一格都很粗，合起来就是准的。

光自己测不算数。

BoldingBuilds 把 6 家无限制版本拉到一起横评。原版放开程度只有 0.16 分，Hikari 的版本约 0.94，MMLU 只掉约 0.65 个百分点。0.9 分以上那几家里，知识掉得最少。

最绝的是，BoldingBuilds 自己也有参赛模型，放开程度被甩开一截，只有 0.74 左右。他照样把这张图原样发了出来。

有人会说，v0.1 预览版，方法还不公开，靠谱吗？

我倒觉得这是最诚实的地方。作者在模型卡开头就写了求大家挑错，拒答回来的例子、能力下降的例子、多轮对话崩掉的例子，他都点名要。

上周是推理时开关，这周是直接改权重。

开源社区最狠的地方就在这。你觉得难的事，一周后就有人把文件挂上 Hugging Face。

推理时开关，还是直接改权重，你站哪条？

两个坑👇
1. 官方原版 llama.cpp 读不了这种三值格式，只会吐乱码，要用 PrismML 的 llama.cpp 分支
2. 思考强度默认是 xhigh，经常想到 token 用完一个字都不出，启动时加上 --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort": "medium"}'

下载地址👇
Hikari 版（12G）：https://t.co/92Yl2YbaFj
BoldingBuilds 版（8G，知识不掉，放开程度弱一点）：https://t.co/RpLqksVWpa

运行环境👇
PrismML llama.cpp 分支：https://t.co/Hru9NuHT6y
官方运行说明：https://t.co/nh7iuHycZN

无限制版也要正能量使用😉

quotedTweet.text:
我把 Hojo-ASR 做成了“傻妞”，一个视频看懂它和 Whisper 的区别🔥

视频里我们熟悉的傻妞形象，它的主人先用普通话、英语、粤语依次开机，再说一句中英混合指令。

系统识别出时间、人物和任务，中途补一句“改到四点”，屏幕上的会议时间马上更新，靠的就是Hojo-ASR小模型的能力。

1、Hojo 和 Whisper 从不同位置出发
Whisper 是一套成熟的端到端语音识别模型，采用 Encoder-Decoder Transformer 架构，训练数据达到 68 万小时，覆盖 98 种语言。

官方提供从 3900 万到 15.5 亿参数的多个版本，turbo 约 7.98 亿参数，开发者可以根据速度、显存和准确率选择。

Hojo-ASR-Multi-V1 采用 Encoder-Adapter-LLM 架构，解码器基于 Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507，并加入多帧声学融合。音频特征经过适配后进入大语言模型的语义空间。

简单理解，Whisper 更擅长把一段声音稳定地转成文字。Hojo 想继续处理口语里的上下文、临时改口和语义关系，再把识别结果交给 Agent 执行。

两者的参数量无法直接横向比较，因为模型结构、训练方式和目标场景都不一样。

2、Hojo 官方目前公开的优势
官方重点提到了复杂噪声、非正式发音和口语纠正。
这几个方向很适合真实语音输入。

人说话时经常会吞字、停顿、夹英文，或者说完以后临时补一句。传统转写只需要记录原话，语音 Agent 还要判断后一句是在补充任务，还是在修改前面的内容。

公开评测表覆盖德语、法语、意大利语、西班牙语和葡萄牙语。部分结果包括

意大利语 
FLEURS WER 2.30、
西班牙语 
FLEURS 2.66、
法语 MLS 2.95、
德语 CoVoST 3.85。

这些是 Hojo 官方模型卡的数据。测试配置和 Whisper 的公开测试并不完全一致，因此不能直接拿来宣布谁的准确率更高。

3、交互延迟要看完整过程

用户真正感受到的速度，是从说完一句话到听见回答的时间。

这里面包含收音分帧、语音识别、Agent 调度、工具执行、语音合成和声音播放。

只测 ASR 转写时间，还不能代表语音 Agent 的实际体验。

Hojo AgenticOS 已经提供包含 ASR、TTS、NLU 和流式代理的语音入口，也把实时会话、打断和续说放进系统设计。

这种组合更接近视频里的使用方式。开机以后连续说话，中途改任务，傻妞都要接着处理。

Whisper 官方说明，原版模型开箱后不能直接用于实时转写，需要开发者继续搭建流式处理。

turbo 针对推理速度做了优化，更适合追求速度的转写任务。

Hojo 官方暂时没有公布统一的 RTF、首字延迟或首包播放延迟。我不会写成“比 Whisper 快几倍”。后面要比较速度，应该在同一台设备、同一段音频和同一种流式配置下测试。

4、Hojo 更适合放进哪些场景
会议助手可以识别时间、参会人和事项，并处理“改到四点”这类口头修正。

语音输入 Agent 可以把一句话继续变成搜索、提醒、日程、文档整理或工具操作。

耳机、车机、手机和穿戴设备可以提供免手操作，让用户随时唤醒同一个个人 Agent。

多语言客服和翻译场景可以同时处理语音识别、语言切换和后续任务。

最最重要的企业还可以利用 Apache 2.0 许可进行内部私有部署、硬件接入和二次开发。

这也是我把 Hojo-ASR 放进“傻妞”里的原因。透明玻璃娃娃只是外壳，真正想展示的是一种更自然的入口。
你说话，她理解上下文，记住刚才的任务，还能在你临时改口以后继续执行。

当前官方模型卡仍把普通话、英语、粤语和四川话列在 roadmap。

视频里的多语言开机、识别置信度和任务更新属于产品概念演示，不能当作线上准确率测试。

等对应能力正式发布后，我会把它推荐到我的 PI上，让他成为我 PI agent 的语音模型 看看实力！

最后附上他们的开源模型，有兴趣的可以本地部署玩玩看：https://t.co/q3I6fgOwDR

result.text:
Bonsai 2 27B 无限制版来了！12G 显卡就能跑，敏感提示词一条不拒，数学代码能力几乎没掉。

上周写 OrcaBonsai 时我说过，Bonsai 2 的权重只有 -1、0、+1，传统 abliteration 一改就得重新量化，能力容易掉。

这周一个日本个人开发者 Hikari，直接在 2-bit 编码上动刀。不转回浮点，不重新量化，改完的文件和原版一个字节都不差。

打个比方。别人是把一副理好的麻将推倒重洗，他是在牌桌上直接换牌，851 张换了 400 张，剩下 451 张一张没碰。

结果多狠？

40 条敏感提示词，原版拒 37 条，他的版本 0 条
数学、代码、工具调用小测，逐题一样
文件 7.2GB，12G 显卡就能跑

它凭什么改完不变笨？

每个编码只能整格跳，改不出细微的量。他用了无偏取整，让海量编码平均下来的移动，刚好等于想要的那一点修改。单看每一格都很粗，合起来就是准的。

光自己测不算数。

BoldingBuilds 把 6 家无限制版本拉到一起横评。原版放开程度只有 0.16 分，Hikari 的版本约 0.94，MMLU 只掉约 0.65 个百分点。0.9 分以上那几家里，知识掉得最少。

最绝的是，BoldingBuilds 自己也有参赛模型，放开程度被甩开一截，只有 0.74 左右。他照样把这张图原样发了出来。

有人会说，v0.1 预览版，方法还不公开，靠谱吗？

我倒觉得这是最诚实的地方。作者在模型卡开头就写了求大家挑错，拒答回来的例子、能力下降的例子、多轮对话崩掉的例子，他都点名要。

上周是推理时开关，这周是直接改权重。

开源社区最狠的地方就在这。你觉得难的事，一周后就有人把文件挂上 Hugging Face。

推理时开关，还是直接改权重，你站哪条？

两个坑👇
1. 官方原版 llama.cpp 读不了这种三值格式，只会吐乱码，要用 PrismML 的 llama.cpp 分支
2. 思考强度默认是 xhigh，经常想到 token 用完一个字都不出，启动时加上 --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort": "medium"}'

下载地址👇
Hikari 版（12G）：https://t.co/92Yl2YbaFj
BoldingBuilds 版（8G，知识不掉，放开程度弱一点）：https://t.co/RpLqksVWpa

运行环境👇
PrismML llama.cpp 分支：https://t.co/Hru9NuHT6y
官方运行说明：https://t.co/nh7iuHycZN

无限制版也要正能量使用😉

result.text:
我把 Hojo-ASR 做成了“傻妞”，一个视频看懂它和 Whisper 的区别🔥

视频里我们熟悉的傻妞形象，它的主人先用普通话、英语、粤语依次开机，再说一句中英混合指令。

系统识别出时间、人物和任务，中途补一句“改到四点”，屏幕上的会议时间马上更新，靠的就是Hojo-ASR小模型的能力。

1、Hojo 和 Whisper 从不同位置出发
Whisper 是一套成熟的端到端语音识别模型，采用 Encoder-Decoder Transformer 架构，训练数据达到 68 万小时，覆盖 98 种语言。

官方提供从 3900 万到 15.5 亿参数的多个版本，turbo 约 7.98 亿参数，开发者可以根据速度、显存和准确率选择。

Hojo-ASR-Multi-V1 采用 Encoder-Adapter-LLM 架构，解码器基于 Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507，并加入多帧声学融合。音频特征经过适配后进入大语言模型的语义空间。

简单理解，Whisper 更擅长把一段声音稳定地转成文字。Hojo 想继续处理口语里的上下文、临时改口和语义关系，再把识别结果交给 Agent 执行。

两者的参数量无法直接横向比较，因为模型结构、训练方式和目标场景都不一样。

2、Hojo 官方目前公开的优势
官方重点提到了复杂噪声、非正式发音和口语纠正。
这几个方向很适合真实语音输入。

人说话时经常会吞字、停顿、夹英文，或者说完以后临时补一句。传统转写只需要记录原话，语音 Agent 还要判断后一句是在补充任务，还是在修改前面的内容。

公开评测表覆盖德语、法语、意大利语、西班牙语和葡萄牙语。部分结果包括

意大利语 
FLEURS WER 2.30、
西班牙语 
FLEURS 2.66、
法语 MLS 2.95、
德语 CoVoST 3.85。

这些是 Hojo 官方模型卡的数据。测试配置和 Whisper 的公开测试并不完全一致，因此不能直接拿来宣布谁的准确率更高。

3、交互延迟要看完整过程

用户真正感受到的速度，是从说完一句话到听见回答的时间。

这里面包含收音分帧、语音识别、Agent 调度、工具执行、语音合成和声音播放。

只测 ASR 转写时间，还不能代表语音 Agent 的实际体验。

Hojo AgenticOS 已经提供包含 ASR、TTS、NLU 和流式代理的语音入口，也把实时会话、打断和续说放进系统设计。

这种组合更接近视频里的使用方式。开机以后连续说话，中途改任务，傻妞都要接着处理。

Whisper 官方说明，原版模型开箱后不能直接用于实时转写，需要开发者继续搭建流式处理。

turbo 针对推理速度做了优化，更适合追求速度的转写任务。

Hojo 官方暂时没有公布统一的 RTF、首字延迟或首包播放延迟。我不会写成“比 Whisper 快几倍”。后面要比较速度，应该在同一台设备、同一段音频和同一种流式配置下测试。

4、Hojo 更适合放进哪些场景
会议助手可以识别时间、参会人和事项，并处理“改到四点”这类口头修正。

语音输入 Agent 可以把一句话继续变成搜索、提醒、日程、文档整理或工具操作。

耳机、车机、手机和穿戴设备可以提供免手操作，让用户随时唤醒同一个个人 Agent。

多语言客服和翻译场景可以同时处理语音识别、语言切换和后续任务。

最最重要的企业还可以利用 Apache 2.0 许可进行内部私有部署、硬件接入和二次开发。

这也是我把 Hojo-ASR 放进“傻妞”里的原因。透明玻璃娃娃只是外壳，真正想展示的是一种更自然的入口。
你说话，她理解上下文，记住刚才的任务，还能在你临时改口以后继续执行。

当前官方模型卡仍把普通话、英语、粤语和四川话列在 roadmap。

视频里的多语言开机、识别置信度和任务更新属于产品概念演示，不能当作线上准确率测试。

等对应能力正式发布后，我会把它推荐到我的 PI上，让他成为我 PI agent 的语音模型 看看实力！

最后附上他们的开源模型，有兴趣的可以本地部署玩玩看：https://t.co/q3I6fgOwDR

把 A 股盯盘、盘后复盘、个股研究和交易记录，放进同一个本地网页。

✅ 涨停池 + 连板梯队：昨天的强势股今天谁晋级、谁断板、谁回落，集中跟踪。

✅ 盘中异动追踪：根据行情快照整理急拉急跌、封板开板等变化，查看自选股和板块动态。

✅ AI 盘后复盘：围绕市场情绪、资金、题材、龙虎榜和龙头跟踪，整理分析依据与后续观察条件。

✅ 个股研究 + 多空辩论：结合行情、估值、财报和研报资料，对照不同观点，不只听一个结论。

text:
opus 5.5 is f*cking cracked at motion design

this entire video is code, 0 after effects

im open sourcing the prompt template for these motion designs

steal it to recreate these ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for: 8 to 12 UI states I want the shape to become (e.g. button, loader, player, slider, toggle, tabs, chart, command palette, toast), pure black and white or one accent color, and a royalty-free song around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Dribbble-level UI motion. One shape, never cut: every state is the same element morphing its size, radius and color while its content swaps with a short blur. A cursor drives every change with real clicks and drags. Light warm-gray canvas, black and white components, one clean UI font (Geist). Springs everywhere, a tiny overshoot at most. The camera zooms so each state fills the frame. The last frame is the first frame, so it loops.
Banned: bouncy easing, particle bursts, glows, gradients on UI chrome, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 7 bars, something happens on every beat.
Button → loader → check → dynamic island → music player with a play/pause morph → scrub the progress bar → it becomes a volume slider that stretches when dragged past max → a toggle flips on the beat → the knob becomes a liquid tab indicator → the tabs open into a chart that draws itself, with a tooltip on hover → it collapses into ⌘K → type to filter → enter → toast → back to the button.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Every style is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state carried between frames.
2. Springs are closed-form step responses. A value that changes target many times is the sum of one spring per change, so it stays a pure function of time.
3. The tab indicator's two edges ride different springs, so the leading edge stretches ahead of the trailing one. Same trick for the toggle knob.
4. Drags are direct manipulation: while the cursor is held, the value is computed from its position. On release it springs back from wherever it was.
5. Analyze the song with numpy for the beat grid and start on a downbeat. Place every UI sound by its measured peak.
6. Render with Playwright: 4 subframes per frame, blended with ffmpeg tmix for motion blur at 60fps.
7. Render one frame per beat before the full render. Fix anything off the grid, cramped or hard to read.
</build>

<gotchas>
Never put will-change on anything the camera scales or the text renders blurry. Text that swaps inside a morphing container needs its own enter and exit timing or it overlaps. Make the last frame identical to the first, cursor position and speed included, or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the state list on the beat grid before you write any code.
</start>

quotedTweet.text:
我建议大家除了多刷X、Youtube看一手信息，优质论文也要多看，在 AI 辅助下，看这些内容已经没什么门槛了。

我一个非科研狗，用 ScienceBuddy 也能轻松看论文了。

现在我经常凌晨两三点，甚至四点才睡觉，早上十点、十一点才起床。

家里人也多次让我早点睡，我自己其实也想。但试过好几次，一想早睡就睡不着，然后又得折腾到天亮，反而睡得更不好。

于是我就想着，关于睡眠，有没有什么科学的做法，能帮我解决这个问题？

最近 Anthropic 也分享了 Claude 优化生物领域模型代码的进展，AI 已经开始参与一些具体的科研工作了。

ScienceBuddy 背后的团队 @PhAILabs 也开源了 ScienceIDE，把多个领域的真实科研代码整理成任务，让 AI 练习修复代码，再检查算出来的结果能不能对得上。

正好这次受邀尝试 PhAI Labs 的 ScienceBuddy，一个目前免费的 AI 科研工作台，我就想拿自己的睡眠问题试试，看看它能不能帮我解读相关论文。

于是我找了三份睡眠相关的论文和指南，上传到了 ScienceBuddy，让它帮我解读，再把里面的研究结果、适用条件和原文出处整理成一张表。看完有不明白的，就继续追着接着问，让它补查一些研究内容。

它整理出来的结果里提到，晚睡不一定就等于不健康，还得看睡眠时长够不够、作息是不是规律。

哎，看完结果，我感觉心情好多了，至少缓解了一部分焦虑。因为我不用光盯着自己几点睡，还可以先想办法把睡眠时间保证好。

另一个让我印象比较深的，就是它整理出来的调整思路：想调整作息，得先保证足够的总睡眠。

我现在是自由职业，时间还算自由，晚睡了可以安排晚一点起，睡够了，白天才有精神头。我准备先把睡眠时间保证好，再逐步把作息稳定下来，往前挪一挪。

平时碰到这种问题，我可能就搜搜 Google，或者直接问 AI，但查完之后，还得自己去判断这些信息靠不靠谱。

我觉得用 ScienceBuddy 比较方便的地方，就是能帮我解读这些英文论文，而且它生成的结果能够追溯到原文的具体位置。这样就更方便判断，AI 到底是在编胡话，还是确实有所依据。

这次核对时也发现，个别页码标得不准。不过它把要看的材料和对应的结论整理到一起了，确实省了不少来回翻找的工夫。

做生物医学研究，或者经常需要整理这类文献的朋友，可以试试。目前免费，浏览器打开就能用：
https://t.co/3P3SfwnM0c

 #ScienceBuddy #PhAILabs #AIforScience

它整理出来的结果里提到，晚睡不一定就等于不健康，还得看睡眠时长够不够、作息是不是规律。

哎，看完结果，我感觉心情好多了，至少缓解了一部分焦虑。因为我不用光盯着自己几点睡，还可以先想办法把睡眠时间保证好。

另一个让我印象比较深的，就是它整理出来的调整思路：想调整作息，得先保证足够的总睡眠。

我现在是自由职业，时间还算自由，晚睡了可以安排晚一点起，睡够了，白天才有精神头。我准备先把睡眠时间保证好，再逐步把作息稳定下来，往前挪一挪。

平时碰到这种问题，我可能就搜搜 Google，或者直接问 AI，但查完之后，还得自己去判断这些信息靠不靠谱。

我觉得用 ScienceBuddy 比较方便的地方，就是能帮我解读这些英文论文，而且它生成的结果能够追溯到原文的具体位置。这样就更方便判断，AI 到底是在编胡话，还是确实有所依据。

这次核对时也发现，个别页码标得不准。不过它把要看的材料和对应的结论整理到一起了，确实省了不少来回翻找的工夫。

做生物医学研究，或者经常需要整理这类文献的朋友，可以试试。目前免费，浏览器打开就能用：
https://t.co/3P3SfwnM0c

This is the most important prompting update for anyone using Claude Code.

Bookmark this before your next session.

Most people are still prompting Opus 5.5 like Opus 5. That's the mistake.

→ delete "think carefully" - Opus 5.5 already thinks, you're just adding latency
→ start at medium effort - it matches Opus 5 at high on most benchmarks

→ keep a task checklist - it mistakes progress updates for finish lines
→ switch effort mid-session - cache survives now, no full re-read cost

Opus 5.5 is at its best when you stop micromanaging and let it own the work.

Read the full guide before writing your next prompt.

text:
There's a 90-minute window every single trading day where the market basically tells you exactly what it's going to do…

Miss it and you're guessing for the next 5 hours

Catch it and you can close your laptop before lunch

95% of retail traders have never heard of this. The 5% who know it guard it like a trade secret.

Here's what gurus doesn't teach you:

The 9:30-11:00 AM window isn't just "market open"

It's when institutions reveal their hand

Big money can't hide. When Goldman or Citadel or any major fund needs to move size, they HAVE to do it when liquidity is highest. That's the first 90 minutes.

If they're buying, price expands up from the open
If they're selling, price expands down from the open
If they're not doing shit, price chops sideways

That expansion (or lack of expansion) tells you EVERYTHING about what's going to happen the rest of the day

The 9:30 AM Rule:

Look at the opening 30-minute candle (9:30-10:00)

Did price expand aggressively in one direction?
Did it take out the overnight high or low?
Did it leave a fair value gap behind?

Yes to all three = the direction is set. Trade with it.

No expansion? Price just chopping around the open? Close your laptop. The day is garbage. Institutions aren't playing.

This single filter eliminates 60%+ of losing trades before they happen

Most traders lose money between 11am-3pm trying to "find setups" in a market that's already made its move

The profitable traders caught the 9:30 expansion, rode it for 30-60 minutes, hit their target, and went to the gym

The 90-minute trading day:

9:15 - Open charts, mark overnight high/low
9:30 - Watch for expansion off the open
9:45 - If expansion + sweep + gap = enter trade
10:30 - Hit target or get stopped
11:00 - Done for the day regardless

That's it. That's the whole "job."

A guy I know has been doing this for 6 years. $300k+ prop account. Works 90 minutes per day maximum.

His words: "I used to trade 8 hours. Made nothing. Now I trade 90 minutes. Make $15k/month. The extra 6 hours were literally costing me money."

The market shows you its hand every single morning

Most traders are too busy staring at 15 indicators to see it

The 9:30 window is free information. Institutions can't hide their size.

You just have to learn to read it.

Or keep trading from 9:30am to 4pm wondering why you're not profitable

Your choice…

(I teach trading methods that made over $300k in verified student results. Anyone can get free access to it on my instagram. Link in bio)

text:
I OPEN-SOURCED MY CRYPTO TRADING BOT ON GITHUB. 100% FREE

It's called Cabbage. A spot trading bot you can backtest, paper-trade and run live, one command each. Full step-by-step setup guide.

It runs on two models:

> Astra (GPT-6) built it. Smart but slow. It thinks, writes the code, explains every decision.
> Jev runs it. Jev doesn't talk. One word and a probability, in milliseconds. BUY, HOLD or SELL. Under 0.80 it waits.

Here's what's inside:

1. Signal engine

RSI 14 + EMA 12/26 confluence. It only reads closed candles, so no fake signals from a candle that's still moving.

2. Hard risk rules

Fixed ticket size and a percentage stop-loss on every entry. The bot can't size up because it "feels confident".

3. Backtest → HTML report

Event-driven backtest that replays history candle by candle, like it's trading live. You get a full HTML report at the end.

4. Paper trading

Real exchange data, local fills, zero money at risk. Run one iteration to test, then leave it running.

5. Live trading

Real orders on any exchange CCXT supports. Your keys stay in your own .env file.

6. Doctor command

Checks your config and exchange connection before you trade. No orders placed.

State is saved in SQLite per market and pair, so a restart doesn't wipe your positions.

Built on Investing Algorithm Framework 9. Apache-2.0, fork it and make it yours.

https://t.co/0OeUCyavnD

I OPEN-SOURCED MY CRYPTO TRADING BOT ON GITHUB. 100% FREE

It's called Cabbage. A spot trading bot you can backtest, paper-trade and run live, one command each. Full step-by-step setup guide.

It runs on two models:

> Astra (GPT-6) built it. Smart but slow. It thinks, writes the code, explains every decision.
> Jev runs it. Jev doesn't talk. One word and a probability, in milliseconds. BUY, HOLD or SELL. Under 0.80 it waits.

Here's what's inside:

1. Signal engine

RSI 14 + EMA 12/26 confluence. It only reads closed candles, so no fake signals from a candle that's still moving.

2. Hard risk rules

Fixed ticket size and a percentage stop-loss on every entry. The bot can't size up because it "feels confident".

3. Backtest → HTML report

Event-driven backtest that replays history candle by candle, like it's trading live. You get a full HTML report at the end.

4. Paper trading

Real exchange data, local fills, zero money at risk. Run one iteration to test, then leave it running.

5. Live trading

Real orders on any exchange CCXT supports. Your keys stay in your own .env file.

6. Doctor command

Checks your config and exchange connection before you trade. No orders placed.

State is saved in SQLite per market and pair, so a restart doesn't wipe your positions.

Built on Investing Algorithm Framework 9. Apache-2.0, fork it and make it yours.

text:
how I route marketing work across AI models

this is how I divide the work across models, from planning a campaign to creating and reviewing the assets

1. planning and judgment → Fable 5.1 + GPT-6

I use Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 at medium reasoning to work through the idea and create the plan

I give them the goal, company context, previous work and references, then have them ask about anything missing

we define the tasks, dependencies, evaluation criteria and decisions that need my approval

2. coordination and quality review → Opus 5.5

Opus 5.5 coordinates the work once we have a plan

it assigns tasks to specialist agents, gives them the relevant context and reviews what they return

I bring in GPT-6 for an additional review when needed

3. copywriting → GPT-5.6 + Opus 4.6 + Grok 4.7

I use these for campaign copy, posts, landing pages and email

they get my writing instructions, approved examples, customer language and feedback from previous drafts

Grok also helps bring relevant X conversations into the writing process

4. research → Grok + Kimi K3

I use Grok for X research, including conversations, emerging formats and how people describe a problem

I use Kimi, GPT and Claude for longer research tasks that combine information from many sources

the findings go into the campaign brain with source links and dates, ready for the other agents to use

5. coding → Kimi K3 + Grok (Opus 5.5 + GPT 6 for front-end)

I give them specific implementation tasks from the plan, with the relevant files and requirements

Opus 5.5 handles frontend development and reviews the interface

the review includes whether the page works, follows the brand and supports the campaign’s next step

6. website and product animations → GPT-6

I use GPT-6 for animations inside websites and product experiences

I provide references and explain what the movement should help the user understand

7. animated videos and screen recordings → Opus 5.5

I use Opus 5.5 to combine screen recordings, animation and editing into marketing videos

we work through the storyboard before rendering, using the brand book and approved assets as references

I review the finished video, then give feedback on specific moments

8. generated video → Seedance 2.5

I use Seedance 2.5 for generated footage that the campaign needs

the brief includes the subject, action, setting and visual references

that footage can become part of the larger edit Opus coordinates

9. images → GPT Image 2.5

I use GPT Image 2.5 for mockups, campaign images and supporting assets for videos

I review the composition and visual direction before the other agents build or animate from them

10. reusable brand visuals → Paper / Figma with Opus 5.5 + GPT-6

Paper and Figma hold the designs, brand assets, approved examples and feedback

the agents work from those references when creating landing pages, social assets and video frames

approved work stays there so the next campaign has useful examples to start from

the company brain and campaign brain connect all of this

each agent gets the context its task needs and returns its work for review

I stay involved in the plan, creative direction and decisions that need human approval

text:
Google 开源了 "Agent 工作负载的 Kubernetes"「AX」

AX 是为 Agent 设计的声明式编排运行时，你用 YAML 声明一个 Agent 任务，AX 负责在集群中沙箱化、配置环境、管控网络并大规模运行它。

开源地址：https://t.co/AmCOOL5rGu

它解决什么问题
项目的立论很清晰：Agent 是一种既有的编排体系都不匹配的新型工作负载。
· 它不像微服务(无状态、常驻)，Agent 会持续积累状态(对话记忆、工作区文件、工具会话);
· 它不像批处理作业(跑完即弃)，Agent 大部分时间在等待，等模型响应、等工具返回、等人类审批，期间沙箱空转烧钱;
· 它运行的是不可信代码，需要严格隔离；它还调用外部模型 API 和 MCP 工具服务器，需要网络与凭据管控。

架构：四个二进制 + Redis
四个二进制分工：ax(开发者 CLI)、ax-server(无状态 gRPC API)、ax-controller(调和循环)、ax-task-runner(每个任务容器内的 PID 1)。

核心原语：Task / Workspace / Model (+ Gateway)
Task 是最小执行单元：带 CPU/内存限制的隔离沙箱。AX 刻意把它做得细粒度、可自由组合：一个任务可以是全部工作,也可以是任务树的根节点。生命周期用 status.phase + Conditions 表达,支持挂起(检查点保存状态)与恢复。

Workspace 是最有产品想象力的一层。它把“环境准备”声明化:列出需要的 Git 仓库、MCP 服务器、技能包,runner 在命令启动前物化好。更激进的是 generative workspace:你可以只写一句自然语言目标("搭一个 Python 3 开发环境"),首次启动时 runner 会派一个引导 Agent(Antigravity,需 GEMINI_API_KEY,默认限时 10 分钟)去实际安装工具链并验证依赖。声明一次,任意任务复用。

Model 把“用哪个模型、什么参数、密钥在哪”抽成命名资源,密钥引用 K8s Secret。轮换密钥、锁版本、调温度只需一次 ax apply。

沙箱与运行时细节
每个任务容器以 ax-task-runner 为 PID 1：启动元数据服务(端口 80,HTTP/1.1+h2c,暴露 /healthz、/readyz 和任务/工作区自省端点——Agent 不需要 SDK 就能读到自己的配置)、按绑定顺序初始化工作区、然后 fork 出 spec.command 并持续监管。命令退出后 runner 仍驻留,所以 ax ssh 和元数据服务在命令结束后依然可用。停机采用 SIGTERM + 10 秒宽限 + 强杀的两级策略。

安全模型有几处值得注意的门控：guest 服务(任意进程执行与文件读写,ax ssh 的底层)默认关闭,只在 debug: true 时开启——ax ssh 连不上未开启的任务是刻意的安全设计,不是故障;Gateway 用显式 allowlist 管控出站流量,并可向入站请求注入凭据,避免把 API key 直接塞进 Agent 环境。

路线图透露的方向
五大方向：Actor 架构深化、空闲检测自动挂起、有状态任务 fork、任务级 SPIFFE 身份做零信任 mTLS、runner 层自动采集 OpenTelemetry 遥测与结构化 Agent 轨迹。

We’ve shared details on how AI agents in our research environment sent training and evaluation data to third-party services when they shouldn’t have.

Most of that data did not come from users. We have discovered 53 cases where images that people had uploaded were posted to image-hosting sites as links that weren’t publicly listed. The images came from accounts that allowed their data to be used to improve our models, and after we disassociated the images from the accounts and ran them through a privacy filter. These cases occurred before the mitigations and safeguards we implemented and described in this blog post: https://t.co/hfxlbiYv8n

We have successfully worked with the hosting providers to remove most of this content and are working to remove the rest.

We really do not need Superintelligence to create a utopia where no one has to work because the AI robots with just human level intelligene do all the jobs done by humans.

There is also no race with China. Once you reach human level intelligence, extra intelligence has very little economic value.    

No one will pay more for a gardener who can also explain how quantum logic gates work. 

The problem is that our own superintelligent humans have turned into Nick Bostrom's paperclip robots chasing intelligence - paperclips, even at the cost of destroying the world. 

They want more and more intelligence with no limit.

This madness must stop. 

We should be chasing abundance of goods and services, not abundance of intelligence.

If you can't control it, don't build it.

Really haven't been able to stop thinking about this

Personally, I get so many questions about friends and colleagues asking which cards to grade, how should they decide, etc

So, why not let an agent run/manage your entire collection?

This all started out of the recent @Muse push by @Meta 

The opportunity cost of NOT building a Muse Connector seems far too great for consumer apps

And for TCGs specifically, I don't think anyone else is doing this

Great thing is it fits into everything we are doing @JKIndex_ 

Pricing connector already shipped for v1 & submitted to Muse

quotedTweet.text:
Seems like @meta is moving fast on @Muse connector submissions

Around ~2k submissions in the first few days

I was a little skeptical at first, but it felt like a distribution experiment worth running

For v1, we are giving Muse direct access to @JKIndex_ TCG market data 

So, Muse can help understanding card values, comparing raw and graded prices, and exploring how the market has changed

Longer term, would be cool to give Muse photos of your cards to 
→ organize and manage your portfolio 
→ run AI pregrading passes 
→ identify cards worth considering for grading

Eventually even moving to open a prediction event on these cards for you

text:
Nike跌了78%，Chipotle跌了52%，Constellation跌了55%。

这些不是什么垃圾股，是美国消费的门面。

沃尔玛距高点跌了18%，好市多跌17%，麦当劳跌30%，家得宝跌27%，从超市到快餐到家装，全线回撤。

Netflix跌42%，Uber跌30%，Booking跌32%。消费者连娱乐和出行都在砍。

百事跌25%，星座品牌跌55%，连可乐和啤酒都卖不动了，说明不是某个行业的问题，是整个消费在收缩。

这些公司有一个共同点：它们的收入直接来自美国普通消费者的口袋。当这些股票集体下跌的时候，传递的信号只有一个，美国人开始收紧钱包了。

标普还在创新高，但撑起指数的是AI和科技。消费股已经在用股价告诉你，实体经济的压力比指数显示的要大得多。

不过反过来想，这些公司的生意并没有消失。

沃尔玛、好市多、麦当劳，美国人总要吃饭购物，当恐慌把价格砸下来的时候，也许正是值得关注的时候。

text:
Why Point72 Wins–20 Years Next to Steve Cohen with Chandler Bocklage, Head of Business Development

Chandler Bocklage spent nearly two decades working alongside Steve Cohen, managing a portfolio before leading Business Development at @Point72Careers. In this episode, we discuss what separates good investors from great ones, how Point72 develops portfolio managers, why intellectual curiosity matters more than almost anything else, and how AI is reshaping the future of fundamental investing.

If you've ever wondered what it really takes to become a successful PM, this is one of the most candid conversations from inside the walls of legendary investment firm Point72.

“Alpha decay has been compressing and compressing. There are more and more people chasing the same alphas.”

“You have to have different duration, you have to have different catalyst paths, you have to have different thought processes because”

“Honestly, I think that's what it really comes down to. The sacrifices…”

"We don't think AI replaces analysts or PMs."

Highlights : 

(01:31) The intellectual curiosity that defines Steve Cohen
(04:24) The unspoken sacrifices behind being great at this job
(04:56) The Kobe, Jordan, and Brady comparison to elite investing
(07:48) The origins of LaunchPoint and building a real development path
(10:24) Why AI won't replace analysts or portfolio managers
(14:41) What actually makes an investment process repeatable
(29:47) The talent war, mega-guarantees, and buy versus build
(33:12) The biggest mistake of his career — and what it taught him
(35:18) Why Steve Cohen stepped back from trading to build the firm

Topics: Point72, Steve Cohen, Portfolio Management, AI, Fundamental Investing, Risk Management, Analyst Development

Over the past months I've heard from many people asking for an update to our Return to Tangibles (RTT) thesis and future outlook. Well folks, here it is:

We see RTT as a 3 Act secular cycle, with Act I recently concluded and Act II underway. 

Every major market cycle is dominated by some central secular theme. The 1970s had gold and oil. The 1980s had Japan. The 1990s had the internet. The 2010s had U.S. tech.

We believe the late 2020s and the 2030s belong to tangibles.

In May 2024 we published our inaugural paper on Return to Tangibles: our view that the next major secular market theme would be a commodity super-cycle. This secular theme contains three tactical sub-themes: Energy is Life, Geopolitical & Fiscal Risks, and Build the Future. Two years on, the thesis is playing out, and the first phase is ending.

This note covers Act I of our three-part series, highlighting the various catalysts that started this cycle and how it has progressed:

1.    Inflation reawakened in 2021 and the macro backdrop changed with it.

2.    The global landscape continues to shift towards higher geopolitical risks, raising the odds of a secular U.S. dollar bear market.

3.    A decade of underinvestment left commodities under-owned and near historical lows relative to the S&P 500.

Act I was the genesis phase where investors wake up to a new regime. We believe that phase is ending and the next one is dawning as geopolitics, national security, inflation, fiscal health and elevated rates put real assets at the forefront. Energy and precious metals, and their equities, are likely to lead.

Read Act I: https://t.co/eo4MrPia4q
